uncertainties: Flag rule used: a topic is true for an exam when that exam's 2026 text names it or when it is an inseparable part of something the text names (e.g. AP sums under 'Arithmetic progressions', conditional probability under 'Bayes' theorem'). It is false when it is a distinct item that only the other exam's text names. The 2027 texts are not out yet.

Logarithms (chapter flagged Adv-only): Main Unit 7 names 'logarithmic functions' and Unit 8 integrates them, so the definition of a logarithm and the log function/graph are marked in_main true. The laws of logarithms, change of base and log equations/inequalities are not named by Main and are marked false, though Main problems assume them as prerequisite skills.
Logarithms: Advanced says only 'Logarithms and their properties'. 'Equations and inequalities using log properties' is included as an application of those properties, not a separately named item.

Trigonometric Equations (chapter flagged Adv-only): the Main 2026 text (Unit 14) names only identities, trigonometric functions and inverse trigonometric functions, so every topic is in_main false. Not verified here, but Main papers set after the 2024 cut may still include trig-equation questions; check recent paper analyses before skipping it for Main.

Trigonometric Ratios: Main says only 'trigonometrical identities and trigonometrical functions'. Compound, multiple/sub-multiple angle and sum-product formulae are treated as identities, and periodicity/graphs as part of 'trigonometric functions' plus Unit 7 'graphs of simple functions', so they are in_main true. This differs from the chapters file note that Advanced 'adds' them.

Conics: Main names only 'equations of conic sections (parabola, ellipse and hyperbola) in standard forms'. Focus, directrix, latus rectum and eccentricity are marked in_main true because the standard forms are defined by them (NCERT); parametric forms, tangents and normals are marked in_main false. 'Sections of a cone' is named only in Main and was placed under Parabola as the first conic.
Power set is named only in Main; Advanced says 'sets and their representations, different kinds of sets', so it is marked in_advanced false. It is a minor topic either way.
Area of a triangle using determinants is named only in Main, so in_advanced false (Advanced students still use it in coordinate geometry).
Rate of change of quantities is named only in Main, so in_advanced false.

Properties of determinants: Main 2026 says only 'evaluation of determinants'; coaching sources say properties were cut from Main in 2024, so in_main false. Advanced says 'properties of these matrix operations', read as covering determinant properties.

Items marked in_main false that Main papers may still touch indirectly: polar form of complex numbers, symmetric functions of roots, L'Hospital's rule, modulus/greatest-integer functions, mean and variance of a random variable, Venn-diagram counting problems. None is named in the Main 2026 text.

Cartesian product is not named in Main but a relation is defined as a subset of it, so in_main true. Conjugate of a complex number is treated as part of Main's 'algebra of complex numbers'. Independent events and total probability are treated as part of Main's 'multiplication theorem' and 'Bayes' theorem'.
AM-GM relation is named in Main; Advanced names 'arithmetic and geometric means' without the inequality. Marked in_advanced true.

Main Unit 8 lists 'evaluation of simple integrals of the type ...' but the formulas were lost in PDF text extraction. The two special-integral topics follow the standard NTA list (1/(x^2 +- a^2), 1/sqrt(x^2 +- a^2), 1/(a^2 - x^2), 1/sqrt(a^2 - x^2), 1/(ax^2+bx+c), (px+q)/(ax^2+bx+c) and root forms, sqrt(a^2 +- x^2), sqrt(x^2 - a^2)); confirm against the PDF.
Matrix/determinant split follows NCERT: adjoint, inverse and linear systems are under Determinants, not Matrices.
Parametric and logarithmic differentiation are not named in either text; they are taught under the chain rule and log functions and were not listed as separate topics.

Main's chapter split of Unit 7 (functions, limits, continuity, differentiation, applications) and Advanced's 'Differential Calculus' and 'Sets, Relations and Functions' were mapped to the app's coaching-style chapters. Every syllabus item mapped to one of the 31 chapter ids; nothing was left over.
